name: Cascadia Remembered — The Flood Memorial Street Festival
creator: Meridian Flood Remembrance Coalition; founded by Yewande Prochazka-Sato and survivors' families
description: Held annually on the anniversary of the 2149 Great Lakes Overflow — a catastrophic managed-flood event that permanently inundated seventeen the Gray Zone districts and displaced an estimated 300,000 people — Cascadia Remembered is a two-day street festival blending grief, resilience, and community celebration. The festival occupies the Floodmark District, built atop the original flood line, and features waterline murals updated each year by community artists, oral history stations, communal meals, and an evening lantern ceremony in which handmade lights are floated on the reclaimed lake. The event is entirely community-funded and explicitly refuses corporate sponsorship.
medium: physical / community neural broadcast / AR overlay (floodline historical mapping)
cultural_impact: Cascadia Remembered is the primary annual act of public memory for the Overflow — an event that corponation-sponsored history tends to minimize or reframe as a managed infrastructure response rather than a preventable disaster affecting the poorest residents.
controversy: Each year, the festival's oral history stations collect new testimony, and the 2219 collection included firsthand accounts alleging that early flood warnings were deliberately withheld from the Gray Zone districts to allow Tier 3-4 property owners time to relocate; the Coalition has been in a protracted legal dispute with Axiom over the publication of these testimonies.
story_hooks: A survivor giving testimony at the 2224 oral history station recognizes someone in the crowd — a former corponation engineer she has spent twenty years trying to identify as responsible for the delayed flood warnings in her district.

The AR floodline mapping overlay used at the festival has been quietly updated with falsified historical data, subtly shifting the documented flood boundary in ways that would affect ongoing compensation claims — and the change was made by someone with access to the Coalition's systems.

A Spire-based documentary filmmaker arrives to cover Cascadia Remembered with genuine intentions, but their press credentials were issued by a HelixCorp subsidiary — and the Coalition leadership is divided on whether to allow them access to the testimony archive.
